research.summary: Subset per-candidate work is SHA256d over ~128 fixed blocks plus ~27 variable blocks then full ECDSA recovery then single-block SHA256(compress(Q)). Fixed-prefix midstate is already shipped in .bin. Beyond within-candidate schedule packing, the remaining untried SHA/dataflow levers are (1) never materializing the ~1.7KB variable section and (2) ordering skip sets for shared-variable-prefix SHA-state reuse. Both are hypotheses only; EC recovery still runs fully per candidate and SHA outputs remain pseudorandom so no EC-table or curve-delta reuse follows.

findings.title: Gather-direct variable-section SHA256d without materializing 1.7KB preimage
findings.mechanism: Starting from the shipped fixed-prefix SHA state, compute the ~27 variable-block compressions by gathering 10B dummy_sigs entries and tail bytes directly into the 16-word ring schedule path, never building/storing/loading the ~1.7KB variable section in global memory. Table lives in constant/shared/broadcast-friendly location; per-thread compress uses ring W reuse.

sources.supports: Variable-section size/location and that fixed-state reuse is already architected; remaining per-candidate cost is variable blocks

findings.new_vs_memory: Distinct from reviewed schedule packing (within-candidate W packing), sparse33-byte SHA, paired SHA, ldcg/fused tails, streaming stores and producer overlap which still assume a materialized variable section or tail path. Memory records no gather-direct no-materialization variant. Not a rename of epoch reuse/ranked specialization.
findings.large_gain_case: Removed work: per-candidate build plus global store/load of ~1.7KB variable preimage and its re-read by SHA. Added work: per-block gather address ALU and small-table broadcast/shared reads plus ring-schedule compute unchanged. Large only if variable-section DRAM traffic is on the critical path at scale; EC chain unchanged so Amdahl-limited.
findings.risks: Divergent gather indices serialize constant path and can add shared/bank or occupancy pressure at 128-reg prepare; table placement must be proven broadcast-friendly; correctness must preserve exact dummy order, padding and SHA256d lengths.
findings.falsification: Mac-only: CPU reference that gathers dummy table on the fly bit-matches CPU grind digests on random skip sets; stub-compile reg/shared estimate only, no timing claim.

findings.title: Prefix-coherent skip ordering with cross-candidate variable-prefix SHA-state reuse
findings.mechanism: Enumerate 9-of-150 skip sets in genlex/prefix-partitioned or revolving-door order so candidates sharing the same early kept/skipped dummies are consecutive, then reuse intermediate SHA states after shared variable blocks instead of recompressing every variable block from the fixed midstate. EC recovery and final SHA256(compress(Q)) still run fully; only shared-prefix compressions are skipped via checkpoint load.

findings.new_vs_memory: Distinct from rejected Gray-code curve shortcut: claims only SHA-state prefix reuse, explicitly no point-delta or scalar-linearity shortcut since z=SHA256d destroys relations and both recids still need full recovery. Distinct from ranked specialization/epoch reuse and from under-1% window-family SHA scan which did not reorder enumeration for prefix sharing.
findings.large_gain_case: Removed work: recompression of shared leading variable blocks for consecutive candidates in the same prefix group. Added work: checkpoint state store/load, grouping/ordering constraint, reduced independent parallelism and possible occupancy loss. Large only for groups with long shared prefixes and if variable SHA is a measurable fraction; no EC-table reuse because scalars stay pseudorandom.
findings.risks: SHA fraction may be small vs EC fixed-base chain so end-to-end gain bounded; grouping harms parallelism and load balance; checkpoint traffic can exceed saved compressions; must not replay hits or bias coverage.
findings.falsification: Mac-only: enumerate skip sets in proposed order on CPU, measure shared-prefix-block histogram and checkpoint bytes vs recompute blocks; verify SHA256d equality vs reference; no GPU timing claim.

research.next_question: What fraction of subset pipeline time is variable-section build plus ~27-block SHA256d versus EC fixed-base chain, and what average shared-prefix length does a genlex/revolving-door 9-of-150 order actually yield without harming parallelism?
